---
title: "Gender-based violence"
description: "Experience of sexual violence, victims of recorded sexual offences, and violence by partners and former partners."
---

In the CSO's Sexual Violence Survey in 2022, 52% of women and 28% of men said they had experienced sexual violence at some point in their lives, as a child or as an adult. The share was highest among young women, at 65% of women aged 18 to 24.

{{< chart gender-sexual-violence-lifetime >}}

## Recorded sexual offences

Most sexual violence is never reported to An Garda Síochána. Of the victims of sexual offences that were recorded in 2025, 2,382 were women and girls, 80% of all victims, compared with 1,781 in 2016. Around 30% of them reported the offence a year or more after it happened. Changes over time can reflect changes in reporting as well as in offending.

{{< chart gender-sexual-offence-victims >}}

## Violence by partners and former partners

Women and girls who are victims of recorded assaults, threats and harassment are much more likely than men and boys to know the suspected offender. In 2024, a current or former partner was the suspected offender for 29% of female victims, compared with 3% of male victims. For men and boys, the suspected offender was most often a stranger.

{{< chart gender-assault-relationship >}}

## Figures by area

The CSO does not publish victims of sexual offences, or victims by sex, for counties or Garda divisions, so these figures cannot be shown on a map. Recorded crime by Garda division is on the [crime by area](../crime/divisions.qmd) page.

The [National Women's Council](https://togetherforpublic.nwci.ie/resources/) and [Rape Crisis Ireland](https://www.rapecrisisireland.ie/) publish further research on gender-based violence in Ireland.
